# Normal Submode Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** A Great Holy Grail War can be fought under the Normal ruleset — seven generic Servants and their Masters per faction, stats generated by the Normal dice, class skills expressed as fixed dice, and the difficulty levels switching the rules they name off.

**Architecture:** Normal is a **stat layer plus a content pack**, not a second engine. Almost every rule the Normal rulebook states is already running, because Advanced shares it. A parallel setup-roll plan, two schema repairs, a difficulty gate and a new compendium is the whole delta.

**Tech Stack:** Foundry VTT v14, vanilla ESM, vitest, YAML content compiled by `tools/build-packs.mjs`.

**Spec:** [`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-09-normal-submode-design.md`](../specs/2026-09-09-normal-submode-design.md)

**Depends on:** [`2026-09-09-war-setup.md`](2026-09-09-war-setup.md) must be complete. It introduces `MatchData.ruleset`, unifies the difficulty vocabulary, adds `servantCatalogue({ruleset})` and `rulesetOfPack`, and — pulled forward from this spec — already delivers `MasterData.baseAttack` and `packs/_source/masters/master-advanced.yml`. **Do not redo those.**

## Global Constraints

- Every constraint in the war-setup plan's Global Constraints section applies here unchanged: the layer rule, the localization prefix rule, the template helper allowlist, SCSS build, documentation in `docs/00-44` **and** `docs/45`, and the commit trailer.
- **Content is YAML, one document per file**, under `packs/_source/<dir>/`. The directory picks the destination pack via `PACKS` in `tools/lib/content.mjs`. `_id`s are `sha1("fgt:" + contentId)`, so **renaming a content id is a breaking change**.
- **The compiler is the gate on what survives.** `actorSystem(doc)` and `itemSystem(doc)` in `tools/lib/content.mjs` are field allowlists; anything not named there compiles to its schema default, silently. If a new field does not appear on a built document, that list is why.
- **Rebuilding packs requires the world shut down.** The application holds the LevelDB open even after the world closes in the browser, so a bare `npm run build:packs` fails `EBUSY`. Use `node tools/fgt-rebuild.mjs`, which shuts down, builds, relaunches and rejoins.
- **Every YAML file quotes the rulebook sentence it implements** in a comment beside the clause. That is why this content is YAML and not JSON.
- Source sheets: `char_orig_sheets/extra docs/Normal Great Holy Grail War.md` (rules) and `Character Sheet - Blue Faction (Normal).md` (statblocks).
- **Normal Servants state no parameter ranks.** That is load-bearing: `domain/base-attack.mjs#baseAttackFor` keeps the authored `baseAttack` only where there is no rank to derive from, and `ServantData#prepareBaseData` fills `health.max` from `baseHealth` only where no END rank is stated. Never add a rank to a Normal sheet.
- **Targeting anchors and shapes are a closed vocabulary**, `TARGET_ANCHORS` and `TARGET_SHAPES` in `module/rules/targeting/vocabulary.mjs`, and `resolveTargets` throws a `RangeError` on anything else. The ones this plan uses:

  | Anchor | Means |
  |---|---|
  | `self` | centred on the caster |
  | `selfEdgeAdjacent` | a chosen orthogonal direction next to the caster; sets `anchor.direction`, which is what makes a `rect`, `line` or `orientedRect` project outward instead of centring |
  | `withinRange` | a free panel the player picks, with `range` and optional `minRange` |

  | Shape | Fields |
  |---|---|
  | `unit` | — (one target) |
  | `square` | `size` |
  | `rect` | `w`, `h` |
  | `orientedRect` | `short`, `long` — **not** `w`/`h`; the direction decides which is which |
  | `line` | `length`, plus optional `diagonalLength`, `bidirectional`, `width` |

  `line` already carries `diagonalLength` and `bidirectional`, so Lancer's *"if diagonal, 1x3"* and Rider's *"in both directions (front and back)"* need no new machinery.

```js
import { describe, it, expect } from "vitest";
import { normalServantSetupPlan, normalMasterSetupPlan } from "../../module/rules/setup-rolls-normal.mjs";
import { resolveSetupPlan } from "../../module/rules/setup-rolls.mjs";

const sheet = (over = {}) => ({ baseHealth: 750, classContainer: "berserker", ...over });
const line = (plan, id) => plan.lines.find((l) => l.id === id);
const resolved = (plan, rolls, signs = {}) => {
  const out = resolveSetupPlan(plan, rolls, signs);
  return (id) => out.find((l) => l.id === id)?.value;
};

describe("normalServantSetupPlan", () => {
  it("rolls Max Health as the Base Health plus or minus 10d20", () => {
    const plan = normalServantSetupPlan(sheet());
    expect(line(plan, "maxHealth").base).toBe(750);
    expect(line(plan, "maxHealth").roll).toEqual({ formula: "10d20", signCoin: true });
  });

  it("adds on Heads and subtracts on Tails", () => {
    const plan = normalServantSetupPlan(sheet());
    expect(resolved(plan, { maxHealth: 87 })("maxHealth")).toBe(837);
    expect(resolved(plan, { maxHealth: 87 }, { maxHealth: true })("maxHealth")).toBe(663);
  });

  it("rolls Max Agility as 1d10 over a base of 10", () => {
    const plan = normalServantSetupPlan(sheet({ classContainer: "saber" }));
    expect(line(plan, "maxAgility").base).toBe(10);
    expect(line(plan, "maxAgility").roll).toEqual({ formula: "1d10" });
  });

  it("applies every Agility class delta the rulebook states", () => {
    const agility = (c) => line(normalServantSetupPlan(sheet({ classContainer: c })), "maxAgility").base;
    expect(agility("lancer")).toBe(12);
    expect(agility("rider")).toBe(11);
    expect(agility("caster")).toBe(8);
    expect(agility("assassin")).toBe(13);
    for (const c of ["saber", "archer", "berserker"]) expect(agility(c)).toBe(10);
  });

  it("applies every Luck class delta the rulebook states", () => {
    const luck = (c) => line(normalServantSetupPlan(sheet({ classContainer: c })), "maxLuck").base;
    expect(luck("lancer")).toBe(-2);
    expect(luck("assassin")).toBe(2);
    for (const c of ["saber", "archer", "rider", "caster", "berserker"]) expect(luck(c)).toBe(0);
    expect(line(normalServantSetupPlan(sheet()), "maxLuck").roll).toEqual({ formula: "1d20" });
  });

  it("gives an unknown container no delta rather than throwing", () => {
    expect(line(normalServantSetupPlan(sheet({ classContainer: "ruler" })), "maxAgility").base).toBe(10);

describe("normalMasterSetupPlan", () => {
  it("rolls Max Health as 250 plus or minus 5d20", () => {
    const plan = normalMasterSetupPlan({}, { mode: "rankless" });
    expect(line(plan, "maxHealth").base).toBe(250);
    expect(line(plan, "maxHealth").roll).toEqual({ formula: "5d20", signCoin: true });

    const plan = normalMasterSetupPlan({}, { mode: "rankless" });

    expect(line(plan, "maxLuck").roll).toEqual({ formula: "1d20" });
  });

  it("gives every Master Base Attack (MAG) 100 when ranks are not in play", () => {
    const plan = normalMasterSetupPlan({}, { mode: "rankless" });
    expect(resolved(plan, {})("baseAttackMag")).toBe(100);
    expect(line(plan, "rank")).toBeUndefined();
  });

    const plan = normalMasterSetupPlan({}, { mode: "coinFlip" });
    expect(line(plan, "rank").roll).toEqual({ formula: "1d2", map: ["A", "C"] });
    expect(resolved(plan, { rank: 1 })("baseAttackMag")).toBe(125);
    expect(resolved(plan, { rank: 2 })("baseAttackMag")).toBe(100);
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Write the Normal plans**

Create `module/rules/setup-rolls-normal.mjs`:

```js
/**
 * @file The Normal ruleset's setup rolls.
 * @see docs/14-checks-and-randomness.md §14.9
 * @see char_orig_sheets/extra docs/Normal Great Holy Grail War.md
 *
 * Layer 2 (rules). Pure — it says what to roll and how to combine the results,
 * and the caller rolls. Same contract as `setup-rolls.mjs`, and deliberately
 * the same LINE VOCABULARY: `signCoin`, `map`, `derivedFrom`, `base` and
 * `roll.formula` all exist already, because the Advanced Master's Max Health is
 * itself a coin-signed `2d100` and its rank line already maps a `1d2` onto
 * letters. Nothing here is a new kind of line; only the numbers differ.
 *
 * The line IDS are shared too — `maxHealth`, `maxAgility`, `maxLuck`,
 * `rank`, `baseAttackMag`, `commandSpells` — which is what lets
 * `engine/summon.mjs#sheetPatch` and `SETUP_PATHS` consume a Normal plan
 * without knowing it is one.
 *
 * Why a separate file rather than a branch inside `setup-rolls.mjs`: the two
 * rulesets derive from different things entirely. Advanced reads rank tables
 * and has no Health roll at all (*"Health(S) is not used"*); Normal rolls
 * Health and reads no table. A single function switching on a flag would be two
 * functions sharing a name.
 */

import { lookup } from "../domain/tables.mjs";

/**
 * Everything a Normal Servant's summon needs rolled.
 *
 * > *"For every Servant, Flip a Coin, then Roll for Health(S). If Heads, the
 * > Max Health is the Base Health plus the rolled value. If Tails, the Max
 * > Health is the Base Health minus the rolled value."*
 *
 * Unlike Advanced, Health **is** rolled here, and it is the reason the Normal
 * sheets state a flat Base Health instead of an END rank.
 *
 * @param {object} sheet the compendium Servant's system data
 * @returns {{kind: "servant", lines: object[]}}
 */
export function normalServantSetupPlan(sheet) {
  const container = sheet?.classContainer ?? "";
  const agilityDelta = lookup("normalAgilityByClass", container) ?? 0;
  const luckDelta = lookup("normalLuckByClass", container) ?? 0;

  return {
    kind: "servant",
    lines: [
      {
        id: "maxHealth",
        label: "Max Health",
        base: sheet?.baseHealth ?? 0,
        roll: { formula: "10d20", signCoin: true },
      },
      {
        id: "maxAgility",
        label: "Max Agility",
        // "Roll for Agility (S): 1d10+10" -- the +10 is a flat base, so the
        // class delta joins it rather than modifying the die.
        base: 10 + agilityDelta,
        roll: { formula: "1d10" },
        note: agilityDelta !== 0 ? `${container} ${agilityDelta > 0 ? "+" : ""}${agilityDelta}` : null,
      },
      {
        id: "maxLuck",
        label: "Max Luck",
        base: luckDelta,
        roll: { formula: "1d20" },
        note: luckDelta !== 0 ? `${container} ${luckDelta > 0 ? "+" : ""}${luckDelta}` : null,
      },
    ],
  };
}

/**
 * The same for a Normal Master.
 *
 * > *"Optional: High Rank & Low Rank Masters — If everyone agrees, you can
 * > determine whether each Master is High Rank or Low Rank by Flipping a Coin
 * > for each Master; Heads=High Rank, Tails=Low Rank. If not, all Masters have
 * > Base Attack (MAG)=100."*
 *
 * That is exactly the `masterMode` setting's `coinFlip` and `rankless` modes,
 * and `rules/master-rank.mjs` already grants the High Rank's three benefits
 * (Base Attack 125, ZON +1, Sustainability +1◈), so this plan only has to
 * decide the rank and let the rank decide the rest.
 *
 * @param {object} sheet
 * @param {{mode?: string}} [options]
 * @returns {{kind: "master", mode: string, lines: object[]}}
 */
export function normalMasterSetupPlan(sheet, { mode = "rankless" } = {}) {
  return {
    kind: "master",
    mode,
    lines: [
      { id: "maxHealth", label: "Max Health", base: 250, roll: { formula: "5d20", signCoin: true } },
      // "Roll for Agility (M): 1d12" and "Roll for Luck: 1d20", both with no
      // flat base -- unlike the Advanced Master, which starts at 4 and 8.
      { id: "maxAgility", label: "Max Agility", base: 0, roll: { formula: "1d12" } },
      { id: "maxLuck", label: "Max Luck", base: 0, roll: { formula: "1d20" } },
      // BEFORE the Base Attack line, which derives from it: `resolveSetupPlan`
      // walks the lines in order and a `derivedFrom` reads what is already
      // resolved.
      ...(mode === "coinFlip"
        ? [{ id: "rank", label: "Rank", base: "", roll: { formula: "1d2", map: ["A", "C"] } }]
        : []),
      baseAttackLine(sheet, mode),
      { id: "commandSpells", label: "Command Spells", base: 3, roll: null },
    ],
  };
}

/**
 * Base Attack (MAG), which is where the Master's rank shows up.
 *
 * Derived from the `rank` line rather than rolled again, so the two can never
 * disagree — a Master who flipped Heads must not end up with 125 and be
 * Rankless for ZON, Sustainability and the Kill Yourself price.
 *
 * @param {object} sheet
 * @param {string} mode
 * @returns {object}
 */
function baseAttackLine(sheet, mode) {
  const label = "Base Attack (MAG)";
  if (mode === "coinFlip") {
    return {
      id: "baseAttackMag", label, base: 0, roll: null,
      derivedFrom: "rank", map: { A: 125, B: 125, C: 100, D: 100 }, fallback: 100,
    };
  }
  // "If not, all Masters have Base Attack (MAG)=100." An Essence-driven rank is
  // an Advanced concept; a Normal table that has not opted into the coin has no
  // ranks at all.
  return { id: "baseAttackMag", label, base: 100, roll: null, note: "no ranks in play" };
}
```

- [ ] **Step 5: Dispatch on the ruleset**

Add to the end of `module/rules/setup-rolls.mjs`:

```js
import { normalServantSetupPlan, normalMasterSetupPlan } from "./setup-rolls-normal.mjs";

/**
 * The setup-roll plans a ruleset uses.
 *
 * One import site for both callers, so `engine/summon.mjs` never has to know
 * which ruleset it is in beyond passing the name through. An unknown ruleset
 * reads as Advanced: a world with a corrupt setting must roll SOMETHING sane
 * rather than nothing at all.
 *
 * @param {string} ruleset
 * @returns {{servant: Function, master: Function}}
 */
export function plansFor(ruleset) {
  return ruleset === "normal"
    ? { servant: normalServantSetupPlan, master: normalMasterSetupPlan }
    : { servant: servantSetupPlan, master: masterSetupPlan };
}
```

Replace `needsSetupRolls` with:

```js
export function needsSetupRolls(sheet, ruleset = "advanced") {
  const unrolled = (stat) => !(sheet?.[stat]?.max > 0);

  // Normal states NO parameter ranks, so the Advanced test below -- "a rank is
  // stated and the stat is unrolled" -- is false for every Normal Servant that
  // ever existed, and `ensureSetupRolls` would never flag one. A zero Agility
  // maximum is the number you must roll UNDER, so it auto-fails every Evade;
  // this is exactly the failure this function was written to catch.
  if (ruleset === "normal") return unrolled("agility") || unrolled("luck");

  const stated = (parameter) => Rank.parseOrNull(sheet?.parameters?.[parameter]) !== null;
  return (stated("agi") && unrolled("agility")) || (stated("luc") && unrolled("luck"));
}
```

```js
  // The Master's own ZON stat is the floor: a Master sheet that states a number
  // is stating it, and the derivation fills in a sheet that does not.
  //
  // The rank bonus is added to BOTH sides. It used to sit only inside
  // `derived`, on the reasoning that a stated ZON should not swallow a rank
  // bonus -- which is exactly what it did whenever the stated figure was the
  // larger one. Inert in Advanced, where almost no Master states a ZON at all;
  // fatal in Normal, where EVERY Master does (Caster 5, Archer and Assassin 4,
  // the rest 2), so a High Rank Normal Master would have bought nothing with
  // the coin that made them one.
  const derived = radius + exclusive + stacking + rankBonus;
  return Math.max(derived, (master?.zon ?? 0) + rankBonus);
```

- [ ] **Step 5: Fix the Command Spells path**

`MasterData.commandSpells` is a plain `NumberField`, and `SETUP_PATHS` maps the line to
`system.commandSpells.value` — a subfield of a number, which Foundry discards. Confirmed live in
`fgt2026`: writing `system.commandSpells.value = 1` to a Master left it at 3.

In `module/engine/summon.mjs`, in `SETUP_PATHS`:

```js
  // `system.commandSpells`, NOT `.value`. The field is a plain NumberField and
  // Foundry drops a write to a subfield of one -- measured live: setting
  // `system.commandSpells.value` to 1 left the Master at 3. Inert until now
  // only because the line's value and the schema's initial are both 3, so any
  // OTHER answer -- an Essence granting a fourth, a house rule -- has been
  // silently discarded.
  commandSpells: "system.commandSpells",
```

```bash
await m.update({ 'system.commandSpells': 1 });
const after = m.system.commandSpells;
```

```yaml
# packs/_source/masters/master-normal.yml
# Conversion source: char_orig_sheets/extra docs/Character Sheet - Blue Faction (Normal).md
#
# The seven Normal Master sheets are identical but for ZON, which varies with
# the Servant they are contracted to (Caster 5, Archer and Assassin 4, the rest
# 2). One template, and `engine/war-setup.mjs#createMasterFor` writes the
# container's figure onto `system.zon` -- which needs no rule change, because
# `zonRadius` already reads the stored value as a floor.
schema: 1
id: master-normal
name: Master
type: master

# "Base Health: 250" -- the same flat figure the Advanced Master carries, before
# the coin-flipped 5d20 of `normalMasterSetupPlan`.
baseHealth: 250
mov: 2
range: { panels: 2, targets: 1 }
# "Base Attack (STR): 50, Base Attack (MAG): 100". The MAG figure is overwritten
# by the setup plan when the table has opted into the High/Low Rank coin.
# "Note: All Masters use Base Attack (MAG) to Attack."
baseAttack: { str: 50, mag: 100 }
rank: ""
commandSpells: 3
# The template's floor. Overwritten per container at commit.
zon: 2

abilities:
  - { ref: normal-magic-crest }

notes: |
  Named `Master` rather than `Master of X`: the setup wizard renames each copy
  after the container it is assigned to.
```

- [ ] **Step 5: Author the Magic Crest**

Create `packs/_source/abilities/normal-magic-crest.yml`:

```yaml
# char_orig_sheets/extra docs/Character Sheet - Blue Faction (Normal).md
#
# > "(Master) Magic Crest — Damage Spell. Deals 2x damage. *Categorized as
# > Noble Phantasm.* Cooldown: 2◈ Turns"
#
# `categorizedAsNP` rather than `isNP`: it is a Skill that COUNTS as a Noble
# Phantasm for every rule that asks -- Magic Resistance's doubled dice, the
# "including NP" reductions, `CS: Force Noble Phantasm` -- without being one for
# the purposes of a Servant's NP uses, which a Master does not have.
schema: 1
id: normal-magic-crest
name: "Magic Crest"
source: class
slug: magicCrest
kind: skill
categorizedAsNP: true
cooldown: { max: "2◈" }
description: |
  (Active) Damage Spell. Deals 2x damage. Categorized as Noble Phantasm.
  Cooldown: 2◈ Turns.
targeting:
  anchor: { kind: withinRange, range: 2, metric: chebyshev }
  shape: { kind: unit }
  selection: { relations: [enemy], chooser: attacker, includeSelf: false }
damage:
  component: mag
  multiplier: 2
phases:
  - kind: damage
  - kind: cooldown
```

### Tasks 4–10: the seven Servants, one per task

Each of these seven tasks authors **one** container's Servant, its class skills and its Noble
Phantasm(s), and ends by looking at that one sheet in the live world. They are independent of one
another and may be executed in any order or in parallel.

**Shared shape for all seven.** Every Servant file lives in `packs/_source/servants-normal/`, every
ability in `packs/_source/abilities/` under a `normal-` id, and every file opens with:

```yaml
# char_orig_sheets/extra docs/Character Sheet - Blue Faction (Normal).md
schema: 1
```

**Shared statblock rules for all seven.** State `baseHealth`, `mov`, `range`, `baseAttack`,
`sustainability`, `classContainer` and `servantClasses`. **State no `parameters` block at all** —
that absence is what makes `baseAttackFor` keep the authored figure and `prepareBaseData` fill
`health.max` from `baseHealth`. State `normalAttack: { mode: fixed, component: str }` for every
Servant **except Caster**, which is `component: mag`: *"Note: Only Caster uses Base Attack (MAG) for
its Attacks, all other Servants use Base Attack (STR)."*

**Shared verification for all seven.** After authoring, in every task:

```bash
npm run validate:content && node tools/fgt-rebuild.mjs
node tools/fgt-eval.mjs "
await game.settings.set('fgt', 'ruleset', 'normal');
const { prepareSummon, commitSummon } = await import('/systems/fgt/module/engine/summon.mjs');
const p = await prepareSummon({ contentId: '<the id>' });
const a = await commitSummon(p);
return JSON.stringify({
  name: a.name, health: a.system.health, agility: a.system.agility, luck: a.system.luck,
  baseAttack: a.system.baseAttack, mov: a.system.mov, range: a.system.range,
  abilities: a.items.map(i => i.name),
}, null, 1)"
```

Confirm by reading the output that Max Health is `baseHealth ± (10..200)`, that Base Attack is the
authored pair and not a table's, and that every ability named in the task is present. Then open the
sheet in Chrome and **look at it** — a sheet that reports correct numbers and renders wrong is the
failure mode this project keeps hitting.

### Task 4: Saber

**Files:**
- Create: `packs/_source/servants-normal/normal-saber.yml`, `packs/_source/abilities/normal-magic-resistance.yml`, `packs/_source/abilities/normal-saber-np.yml`

**Interfaces:**
- Produces: content ids `normal-saber`, `normal-magic-resistance`, `normal-saber-np`.

- [ ] **Step 1: Author the class skill**

Create `packs/_source/abilities/normal-magic-resistance.yml`:

```yaml
# > "(Saber) Class Skill: Magic Resistance — (Passive) All MAG damage taken is
# > reduced by 5d20; if NP, double the number of dice rolled.
# > <Magic Resistance: 5d20>"
#
# `mode: dice` on a `Resistance` rule element, which is already wired end to
# end: `elements.mjs` projects it, `attack.mjs` doubles the formula when the
# incoming attack is a Noble Phantasm, and `pipeline.mjs` subtracts the rolled
# total and labels it "never negates". Normal's Magic Resistance is a flat pool
# rather than Advanced's rank comparison, so it CANNOT negate -- which is the
# behaviour that path already has.
schema: 1
id: normal-magic-resistance
name: "Magic Resistance"
source: class
slug: magicResistance
kind: classSkill
passive: true
copyable: { allowed: false, reason: classSkill }
description: |
  (Passive) All MAG damage taken is reduced by 5d20; if NP, double the number of dice rolled.
passiveRules:
  - key: Resistance
    component: mag
    mode: dice
    formula: "5d20"
    npDiceDoubled: true
    includesNP: true
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Author the Noble Phantasm**

Create `packs/_source/abilities/normal-saber-np.yml`:

```yaml
# > "(Saber) Noble Phantasm — Hits a 3x3 panel area in any non-diagonal
# > direction next to Saber for 3x damage. Can only be used once.
# > <Noble Phantasm+: [(Base Attack(STR)+5d10)*3]>"
#
# The 5d10 inside the bracket is the Attack+/Attack− pool, which the damage
# pipeline applies at stage 2 -- before the multiplier, which is the placement
# the author's reference calculation requires. It is NOT authored here.
schema: 1
id: normal-saber-np
name: "Noble Phantasm"
isNP: true
kind: noblePhantasm
slug: normalSaberNP
maxUses: 1
description: |
  (Active) Hits a 3x3 panel area in any non-diagonal direction next to Saber for 3x damage.
  Can only be used once.
targeting:
  anchor: { kind: selfEdgeAdjacent }
  shape: { kind: square, size: 3 }
  selection: { relations: [enemy, ally, neutral], chooser: all, includeSelf: false }
  limits: { requiresZon: true }
  isDamagingAoE: true
damage:
  component: str
  multiplier: 3
phases:
  - kind: damage
```

`selfEdgeAdjacent` is what *"in any non-diagonal direction next to"* resolves to: it sets
`anchor.direction`, and `shapes.mjs`'s `rect` branch then projects the block outward from the caster
rather than centring it (`if (anchor.direction) return orthogonalAdjacentRect(...)`). A `square` is a
`rect` with equal sides, so the 3x3 lands in front of Saber, which is the clause.

- [ ] **Step 3: Author the Servant**

Create `packs/_source/servants-normal/normal-saber.yml`:

```yaml
# char_orig_sheets/extra docs/Character Sheet - Blue Faction (Normal).md — "Saber of Blue"
#
# NO `parameters` block, and that absence is load-bearing: `baseAttackFor` keeps
# an authored Base Attack only where there is no rank to derive from, and
# `prepareBaseData` fills `health.max` from `baseHealth` only where no END rank
# is stated. A rank here would silently replace every number below with a
# table's.
schema: 1
id: normal-saber
name: Saber
type: servant

servantClasses: [saber]
classContainer: saber
baseHealth: 1250
mov: 4
range: { panels: 1, targets: 1 }
baseAttack: { str: 200, mag: 150 }
normalAttack: { mode: fixed, component: str }
sustainability: "2◈"

abilities:
  - { ref: normal-magic-resistance }
  - { ref: normal-saber-np }

notes: |
  The setup wizard renames each copy `Saber of <Faction>`; the sheets differ
  across factions only in that word.
```

```bash
`mode: dice` needed no engine work — it has been wired from elements.mjs
```

- [ ] **Step 1: Author Battle Continuation**

Create `packs/_source/abilities/normal-battle-continuation.yml`:

```yaml
# > "(Lancer) Class Skill: Battle Continuation - Damage Reduction — (Passive)
# > All damage taken is reduced by 2d20; if NP, double the number of dice
# > rolled. <Battle Continuation- Damage Reduction: 2d20>"
# > "(Lancer) Class Skill: Battle Continuation - Survival — (Passive) When
# > Health is reduced to 0, roll 5d20 and restore Lancer's Health by that
# > amount. This Skill can only be used once."
#
# Two clauses, one document, because they are one Skill on the sheet and a
# Skill Seal must take both. `DamageNegation` in `mode: dice` with a FIXED
# formula rather than Advanced's rank table; `RevivalSource` with `uses: 1` for
# the survival, which is the element the revival machinery already reads.
schema: 1
id: normal-battle-continuation
name: "Battle Continuation"
source: class
slug: battleContinuation
kind: classSkill
passive: true
copyable: { allowed: false, reason: classSkill }
description: |
  (Passive) All damage taken is reduced by 2d20; if NP, double the number of dice rolled.
  (Passive) When Health is reduced to 0, roll 5d20 and restore Lancer's Health by that amount.
  This Skill can only be used once.
passiveRules:
  - key: DamageNegation
    mode: dice
    formula: "2d20"
    npDiceDoubled: true
    includesNP: true
  - key: RevivalSource
    formula: "5d20"
    uses: 1
```

**Files:**

- [ ] **Step 1: Author Independent Action**

Create `packs/_source/abilities/normal-independent-action.yml`:

```yaml
# > "(Archer) Class Skill: Independent Action - Improved Sustainability —
# > (Passive) When Archer's Master is defeated, Flip a Coin. If Heads, Archer's
# > Sustainability is increased by 3◈ Turns."
# > "(Archer) Class Skill: Independent Action - Contract Denial — (Passive) When
# > an enemy Master or Caster tries to contract Archer, the 'Contract Servant'
# > roll is performed twice. Archer can only be contracted if both rolls are
# > successful."
#
# The Contract Denial clause is NOT authored: `rules/contract.mjs#rollsRequired`
# already returns 2 for a Servant with no Independent Action rank, and
# `contractPlan` already requires ALL rolls to succeed. Advanced's ranks raise
# that to 3, 4 or Infinity; Normal's flat "twice" is the default the function
# already has. Stated in the description so a player reading the sheet sees the
# rule, and implemented by not overriding it.
schema: 1
id: normal-independent-action
name: "Independent Action"
source: class
slug: independentAction
kind: classSkill
passive: true
copyable: { allowed: false, reason: classSkill }
description: |
  (Passive) When Archer's Master is defeated, Flip a Coin. If Heads, Archer's Sustainability is
  increased by 3◈ Turns.
  (Passive) When an enemy Master or Caster tries to contract Archer, the 'Contract Servant' roll is
  performed twice. Archer can only be contracted if both rolls are successful.
passiveRules:
  - key: OnEvent
    event: masterDefeated
    chance: { formula: "1d2", success: [1] }
    then:
      - kind: SustainabilityGain
        amount: "3◈"
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Author the close-combat penalty**

Create `packs/_source/abilities/normal-close-combat-penalty.yml`:

```yaml
# > "(Archer) Close Combat Penalty — (Passive) When Archer performs an Attack at
# > a Range of 1 panel, his Base Attack is halved. This penalty can be negated
# > if Archer receives an Item from Random Events."
#
# A separate document from Independent Action because it is a separate heading
# on the sheet and is not a Class Skill -- a Skill Seal must not take it.
schema: 1
id: normal-close-combat-penalty
name: "Close Combat Penalty"
slug: closeCombatPenalty
kind: skill
passive: true
description: |
  (Passive) When Archer performs an Attack at a Range of 1 panel, his Base Attack is halved.
  This penalty can be negated if Archer receives an Item from Random Events.
passiveRules:
  - key: DamageModifier
    modifierKey: closeCombatPenalty
    direction: dealt
    percent: -50
    includesNP: true
    attackPredicate:
      - "attack:range:1"
      - { not: "self:item:closeCombatNegator" }
```

- [ ] **Step 1: Author Riding**

Create `packs/_source/abilities/normal-riding.yml`:

```yaml
# > "(Rider) Class Skill: Riding - Double Move — (Passive) Rider is able to Move
# > twice during your Turn if it Attacks in that turn. However, the total number
# > of panels Moved during both times cannot exceed Rider's MOV."
# > "(Rider) Class Skill: Riding - Riding Attack — (Passive) As Rider's Normal
# > Attack during its Turn, Rider is able to Attack all enemies in his path
# > while moving in a straight line. ... Rider cannot Attack after it has
# > stopped, and neither can it Move a second time after using a Riding Attack."
# > "(Rider) Class Skill: Riding - Passenger Seat — (Passive) When Rider Moves,
# > Rider's Master is able to Move together with Rider. ... This counts as only
# > Moving one Servant Unit."
#
# All three clauses are ALREADY IMPLEMENTED: `engine/riding.mjs` performs the
# carry and the straight-line attack, `turnState.mayMoveAgain` and
# `turnState.usedRidingAttack` hold the mutual exclusion, and `movedPanels` is a
# running total precisely because Riding's two moves share one MOV allowance
# (Ch. 18 §18.4). What this document does is TURN THEM ON for a Servant with no
# Riding rank -- Normal's Riding has no rank at all.
schema: 1
id: normal-riding
name: "Riding"
source: class
slug: riding
kind: classSkill
passive: true
copyable: { allowed: false, reason: classSkill }
description: |
  (Passive) Rider is able to Move twice during your Turn if it Attacks in that turn. The total
  number of panels Moved during both times cannot exceed Rider's MOV.
  (Passive) As Rider's Normal Attack, Rider is able to Attack all enemies in its path while Moving
  in a straight line. Rider cannot Attack after it has stopped, and cannot Move a second time after
  using a Riding Attack.
  (Passive) When Rider Moves, Rider's Master is able to Move together with Rider. This counts as
  only Moving one Servant Unit.
passiveRules:
  - key: GrantedAbility
    ability: doubleMove
  - key: GrantedAbility
    ability: ridingAttack
  - key: GrantedAbility
    ability: passengerSeat
```

Confirm the three ability slugs against `packs/_source/class-skills/riding.yml` and use whatever
that file names them — it is the Advanced version of the same three clauses, and the slugs must
match or `engine/riding.mjs` will not see them.

- [ ] **Step 2: Author the Noble Phantasm**

Create `packs/_source/abilities/normal-rider-np.yml`:

```yaml
# > "(Rider) Noble Phantasm — Hits a 1x6 or 6x1 panel area in a straight line in
# > both directions (front and back) for 5x damage; if diagonal, 1x5 or 5x1
# > panel area. Can only be used once."
schema: 1
id: normal-rider-np
name: "Noble Phantasm"
isNP: true
kind: noblePhantasm
slug: normalRiderNP
maxUses: 1
description: |
  (Active) Hits a 1x6 or 6x1 panel area in a straight line in both directions (front and back)
  for 5x damage; if diagonal, 1x5 or 5x1 panel area. Can only be used once.
targeting:
  # `selfEdgeAdjacent`, not `self`: the line needs a DIRECTION, and `self`
  # supplies none -- `shapes.mjs` falls back to `DELTA.n` and the Noble Phantasm
  # would fire north for ever. The line still runs through Rider's own panel,
  # because `line` measures from `anchor.casterPanel`.
  anchor: { kind: selfEdgeAdjacent }
  # "in both directions (front and back)" -- the line runs through Rider rather
  # than away from it, which is why this is `bidirectional` rather than a length
  # of 12 in one direction. Both fields are already read by `shapes.mjs`.
  shape: { kind: line, length: 6, diagonalLength: 5, bidirectional: true }
  selection: { relations: [enemy, ally, neutral], chooser: all, includeSelf: false }
  limits: { requiresZon: true }
  isDamagingAoE: true
damage: { component: str, multiplier: 5 }
phases:
  - kind: damage
```

### Task 8: Caster

**Files:**

- [ ] **Step 1: Author Territory Creation**

Create `packs/_source/abilities/normal-territory-creation.yml`:

```yaml
# > "(Caster) Class Skill: Territory Creation - Damage Boost — (Passive) When
# > Caster is within its Home Base, all damage dealt by Caster is increased by
# > 5d20 including NP."
# > "(Caster) Class Skill: Territory Creation - Bounded Field — (Passive) When
# > an allied Master or Servant is Attacked while within Caster's Home Base, all
# > damage taken is reduced by (3d10+20). This effect is lost if Caster is
# > defeated."
#
# `self:inHomeBase` is a board annotation `rules/snapshot.mjs` already sets from
# `inOwnHomeBase`, and the offensive clause keys on where the OWNER stands
# rather than the target -- the bonus applies even to attacks OUT of the base
# (Ch. 19 E5). The defensive clause is an Aura, which is what makes "this effect
# is lost if Caster is defeated" free: an aura with no source contributes
# nothing.
schema: 1
id: normal-territory-creation
name: "Territory Creation"
source: class
slug: territoryCreation
kind: classSkill
passive: true
copyable: { allowed: false, reason: classSkill }
description: |
  (Passive) When Caster is within its Home Base, all damage dealt by Caster is increased by 5d20
  including NP.
  (Passive) When an allied Master or Servant is Attacked while within Caster's Home Base, all damage
  taken is reduced by (3d10+20). This effect is lost if Caster is defeated.
passiveRules:
  - key: DamageModifier
    modifierKey: territoryCreationAtk
    direction: dealt
    mode: dice
    formula: "5d20"
    includesNP: true
    predicate: ["self:inHomeBase"]
  - key: Aura
    radius: null
    zone: homeBase
    relations: [ally, self]
    effect:
      key: DamageNegation
      mode: dice
      formula: "3d10+20"
      includesNP: true
```

### Task 9: Assassin

**Files:**
- Create: `packs/_source/servants-normal/normal-assassin.yml`, `packs/_source/abilities/normal-presence-concealment.yml`, `packs/_source/abilities/normal-assassin-np.yml`

**Interfaces:**
- Produces: content ids `normal-assassin`, `normal-presence-concealment`, `normal-assassin-np`.

- [ ] **Step 1: Author Presence Concealment**

Create `packs/_source/abilities/normal-presence-concealment.yml`:

```yaml
# > "(Assassin) Class Skill: Presence Concealment — (Active) Used during your
# > Turn. Effects last for 2◈ Turns. Cooldown: 1◈ Turns after deactivation.
# > When Active, Assassin cannot be targeted for an attack. When caught within
# > range of an AoE Attack and fails to Evade, Flip a Coin. If Heads, no damage
# > and effects are received. If Tails, Total Damage taken is reduced by 50%
# > including NP, then Presence Concealment is deactivated."
# > "- Hidden Strike — (Passive) Attacks performed while Active cannot be
# > Blocked or Countered; and if Evaded, the Evade roll is increased by 4."
# > "- Assassination — (Passive) While Active, Assassin is able to Attack
# > Masters and Move anywhere regardless of their Servant's position. If
# > Assassin performs an Attack while Active, it is deactivated at the end of
# > the Combat Process."
# > "- Sneak Attack — (Passive) While Active, Assassin deals 2x damage to
# > Servants including NP."
#
# `engine/concealment.mjs` and `rules/concealment.mjs` already carry the whole
# model, including the Master-protection exception Ch. 16 names Presence
# Concealment by. This is a MODE (`isMode`), which is what gives the toggle its
# own rules about when it may be switched (`rules/modes.mjs`).
schema: 1
id: normal-presence-concealment
name: "Presence Concealment"
source: class
slug: presenceConcealment
kind: classSkill
isMode: true
active: false
toggleLock: "1◈"
copyable: { allowed: false, reason: classSkill }
description: |
  (Active) Lasts 2◈ Turns. Cooldown 1◈ Turns after deactivation. While Active, Assassin cannot be
  targeted for an attack; caught in an AoE Attack and failing to Evade, Flip a Coin — Heads, no
  damage or effects; Tails, Total Damage is reduced by 50% including NP and Presence Concealment
  deactivates.
  (Passive) Attacks while Active cannot be Blocked or Countered; if Evaded, the Evade roll is
  increased by 4.
  (Passive) While Active, Assassin may Attack Masters and Move anywhere regardless of their
  Servant's position; an Attack deactivates it at the end of the Combat Process.
  (Passive) While Active, Assassin deals 2x damage to Servants including NP.
cooldown: { max: "1◈", countFrom: deactivation }
activeRules:
  - key: TargetabilityModifier
    untargetable: true
  - key: ForbidReaction
    reactions: [block, counter]
    direction: incoming
  - key: CheckModifier
    check: evade
    direction: incoming
    value: 4
  - key: DamageModifier
    modifierKey: sneakAttack
    direction: dealt
    percent: 100
    includesNP: true
    targetPredicate: ["target:kind:servant"]
  - key: SuppressForeignEffects
    scope: masterProtection
```

Check every `key` above against `Object.keys(EXECUTORS)` in `module/rules/elements.mjs`; the content
validator checks the key and the selector field names, and a misnamed field on a **known** key
passes validation silently forever.

- [ ] **Step 2: Author the Noble Phantasm**

Create `packs/_source/abilities/normal-assassin-np.yml`:

```yaml
# > "(Assassin) Noble Phantasm — Usable after 3◈ Turns have passed. Range=2
# > panels. Hits 1 Unit for 3x damage and inflicts Curse on the DU.
# > Cooldown: 3◈ Turns."
#
# The Assassin statblock reads "NP: N/A" for uses, and the NP text states a
# cooldown rather than a use count -- so it is repeatable on the clock, not
# limited. `npGateRound` carries the "after 3◈ Turns have passed" opening gate.
schema: 1
id: normal-assassin-np
name: "Noble Phantasm"
isNP: true
kind: noblePhantasm
slug: normalAssassinNP
npGateRound: "3◈"
cooldown: { max: "3◈" }
description: |
  (Active) Usable after 3◈ Turns have passed. Range=2 panels. Hits 1 Unit for 3x damage and
  inflicts Curse on the target. Cooldown: 3◈ Turns.
targeting:
  anchor: { kind: withinRange, range: 2, metric: chebyshev }
  shape: { kind: unit }
  selection: { relations: [enemy], chooser: attacker, includeSelf: false }
  limits: { requiresZon: true }
damage: { component: str, multiplier: 3 }
phases:
  - kind: damage
  - kind: applyEffects
    rules:
      - key: OnEvent
        event: damageDealt
        effect: { id: curse }
  - kind: cooldown
```

Create `packs/_source/abilities/normal-mad-enhancement.yml`:

```yaml
# > "(Berserker) Class Skill: Mad Enhancement — (Active) Used during your Turn.
# > Toggles. Cooldown: 2◈ Turns. While Active, Berserker's Master loses 15
# > Health at the end of each Turn Berserker Acts. When Berserker's Master is
# > left with 15 Health or less, Mad Enhancement is forcibly deactivated at the
# > end of the Turn. When Berserker's Master is defeated, Berserker remains in
# > whatever state it was in until contracted to another Master/Caster. While
# > deactivated, Sustainability is 2◈; when activated, 1◈."
# > "- Berserk Rage — (Passive) While Active: 1. All damage taken is reduced by
# > 50% including NP. 2. All STR damage dealt is increased by 100%; halved for
# > MAG damage. 3. Move +2, Range +1 panel. 4. Master's Servant Range +2 panels.
# > 5. Berserker can only Evade with Evade−."
#
# `rules/modes.mjs` already answers the two questions a toggle raises — may it
# be switched, and is it forced — and `toggleLock` is the "2◈ before it can be
# used again" clause. Clause 4 is a ZonBonus that STACKS: Ch. 16's formula
# comment lists madEnhancement as additive rather than in the max-not-sum
# channel.
schema: 1
id: normal-mad-enhancement
name: "Mad Enhancement"
source: class
slug: madEnhancement
kind: classSkill
isMode: true
active: false
toggleLock: "2◈"
copyable: { allowed: false, reason: classSkill }
description: |
  (Active) Toggles during your Turn; 2◈ Turns must pass before it can be used again.
  While Active, Berserker's Master loses 15 Health at the end of each Turn Berserker Acts, and Mad
  Enhancement is forcibly deactivated at the end of the Turn when that Master has 15 Health or less.
  Sustainability is 2◈ while deactivated and 1◈ while Active.
  (Passive) While Active: damage taken −50% including NP; STR damage dealt +100%, MAG +50%;
  Move +2 and Range +1; the Master's Servant Range +2; Berserker may only Evade with Evade−.

  - key: DamageModifier
    modifierKey: berserkRageDefence
    direction: taken
    percent: -50
    includesNP: true
  - key: DamageModifier
    modifierKey: berserkRageOffence

    percent: 100
    npValue: 100
    componentPercent: { str: 100, mag: 50 }
  - key: MovDelta
    value: 2
  - key: RangeDelta
    value: 1
  - key: ZonBonus
    value: 2
    stacks: true
  - key: CheckModifier
    check: evade
    direction: outgoing
    variant: minus
  - key: OnEvent
    event: actedTurnEnd
    then:

        target: contractedMaster
        amount: 15
  # "forcibly deactivated at the end of the Turn" once the Master is at 15 or
  # less. A forced deactivation, not a refusal to activate: `rules/modes.mjs`
  # answers both questions and this is the second.
  - key: Compulsion
    mode: deactivate
    when: turnEnd
    predicate: ["master:health:lte:15"]
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Write the module**

Create `module/rules/difficulty.mjs`:

```js
/**
 * @file What each difficulty level takes out of the game.
 * @see char_orig_sheets/extra docs/Normal Great Holy Grail War.md
 *
 * Layer 2 (rules). Pure.
 *
 * > *"Beginner: Damage modifiers & Luck Check removed. Intermediate: Luck Check
 * > removed. Expert: Nothing removed. Lunatic: Random Event rate up."*
 * > *"To play without damage modifiers, just use Base Attack for damage
 * > calculation instead of Attack+/Attack-."*
 *
 * An unknown level reads as **Expert**, not as Beginner: a corrupt setting must
 * fail towards the full rules rather than quietly switching two of them off,
 * because a missing rule is invisible and an extra one is not.
 *
 * Lunatic removes nothing. Its one mechanical clause — *"there should always be
 * at least 2 Civilians on the board"* — is `rules/environment.mjs#civiliansNeeded`,
 * which has been implemented since it was written against a difficulty value
 * the setting could not produce.
 */

/** Levels that switch the `Attack+`/`Attack−` `5d10` off. */
const NO_DAMAGE_MODIFIERS = Object.freeze(["beginner"]);

/** Levels that switch the Luck Check off. */
const NO_LUCK_CHECK = Object.freeze(["beginner", "intermediate"]);

/**
 * Does the `5d10` damage-modifier roll apply?
 * @param {string|undefined} difficulty
 * @returns {boolean}
 */
export function damageModifiersApply(difficulty) {
  return !NO_DAMAGE_MODIFIERS.includes(difficulty);
}

/**
 * Is a Luck Check offered at all?
 * @param {string|undefined} difficulty
 * @returns {boolean}
 */
export function luckChecksApply(difficulty) {
  return !NO_LUCK_CHECK.includes(difficulty);
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Gate the damage modifier**

In `module/rules/damage/pipeline.mjs`, add `import { damageModifiersApply } from "../difficulty.mjs";`
and at the top of `stage2Crit`, after `s.begin(2)`:

```js
  // "To play without damage modifiers, just use Base Attack for damage
  // calculation instead of Attack+/Attack-." Contributed as an explicit zero
  // with its reason rather than skipped, so the explainer says the roll was
  // removed rather than leaving a gap a reader has to account for.
  if (!damageModifiersApply(s.ctx.difficulty)) {
    s.contribute("attack+", 0, "removed on Beginner", "attacker");
    s.end(2);
    return;
  }
```

`s.ctx.difficulty` must be populated. There are **two** sites that build a damage context, both in
`module/engine/attack.mjs`, each identifiable by its `crit:` line:

- `~2700` — `crit: { isCrit, chanceUsed: critSpec.percent },` (the ordinary resolution)
- `~4752` — `crit: { isCrit: false, chanceUsed: 0 },` (the reflection, which flips no coin)

Add to **both** objects, beside the `crit:` line:

```js
    // Which rolls this table plays with. Threaded into ctx the same way
    // `grandOrder` is, because a pure pipeline stage may not read a setting.
    difficulty: board.difficulty,
```

Both must be changed. Gating only the first would leave a reflected attack rolling a `5d10` on
Beginner, which is the harder of the two to notice.

`module/engine/attack.mjs:1635-1638` already refuses a Luck Check for a different reason, and the


### Task 13: A board holds one ruleset

**Files:**
- Modify: `module/engine/summon.mjs` (`commitSummon`)
- Modify: `lang/en.json`
- Modify: `docs/45-implementation-status.md`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `rulesetOfPack` (war-setup plan, Task 5).
- Produces: `commitSummon` throws when the Servant's pack disagrees with the match's ruleset.

- [ ] **Step 1: Refuse the mismatch**

In `module/engine/summon.mjs#commitSummon`, before building `data`:

```js
  // The wizard filters its catalogue by ruleset, and a stale draft is the case
  // a filter alone does not cover -- a GM who rolled fourteen Advanced Servants
  // and then switched the war to Normal has a draft the filter has already
  // stopped looking at.
  //
  // Refused rather than converted. A Normal Saber's 1250 Health and an Advanced
  // Servant's rank-derived Health are two different scales, and a board holding
  // both is a fight in which neither number means what the other means.
  const warRuleset = game.combat?.system?.ruleset
    ?? game.settings.get("fgt", "ruleset") ?? "advanced";
  const sourceRuleset = rulesetOfPack(prepared.source.pack ?? "");
  if (sourceRuleset !== warRuleset) {
    throw new Error(game.i18n.format("FGT.Summon.RulesetMismatch", {
      name: prepared.source.name, servant: sourceRuleset, war: warRuleset,
    }));
  }
```

`prepared.source.pack` is the compendium collection on a document fetched from a pack. If a
Servant was built some other way and carries no pack, `rulesetOfPack("")` returns `"advanced"`,
which is the right default for a hand-made Servant.

